newsitem.title: UK: Britain postpones Tube privatisation - paper.
newsitem.headline: Britain postpones Tube privatisation - paper.

text.p: Britain has shelved plans to privatise the London underground rail network, fearing a hostile public reaction, the Times reported on Thursday.
The Conservative government had originally planned to announce the privatisation of London's underground network, known as the "Tube", later on Thursday, the newspaper said.
But negative responses to leaked details made the government change its mind, although it still intended to go ahead with selling the Tube before the forthcoming general election, said the Times.
The election must be held before May 22.

The planned Tube sell-off, which drew heavy fire from the opposition Labour Party, could yield between 600 million and 1.5 billion pounds ($960 million and $2.4 billion), former Conservative transport minister Steven Norris told Reuters earlier.
